summary.headline: MM Forgings H1 FY27 sales of about 44,000 tons; capacity rose to 1.30 lakh tonnes with a new 4,000-tonne press at Vizianagaram in Q2.
summary.overview: The transcript is a poor-quality, partly garbled recording of the Q2 FY27 post-results call, so several figures are uncertain. Management cited H1 sales of about 44,000 tonnes, realisation of about 2.34% (unit unclear), and Europe's share rising to about 16.5%. Installed capacity rose from 1.20 lakh to 1.30 lakh tonnes in Q2 after a 4,000-tonne press was added, and machining utilisation was put at roughly 75-80%. The heavy press is expected to start production in Q4 FY27, with management pointing to later volume ramp-up and possible further investment. Average cost of debt was stated as 5.42%, and total debt is to stay around the current level.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst noted roughly 19% sequential improvement in sales per ton; management did not confirm this
Up from 1.20 lakh tonnes in Q2 after adding 4,000-tonne press at Vizianagaram

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 1,000 crore asset base; over Rs 750 crore on forging side (as stated)
about Rs 800 crore spent, Rs 380 crore capitalised (as stated in Q&A)

segments.name: Forgings (auto and CV)
segments.commentary: Management said the company is about 85% dependent on India and rest of world CV markets combined; non-auto is growing as a diversification lever. Europe share was cited as rising to about 16.5%.

segments.name: Machining
segments.commentary: Machining utilisation is around 75-80%, with new machining lines being added for expansions, new products and new customers. Management did not give a total machining capacity figure and said it is a moving number.

segments.name: Heavy press (non-auto)
segments.commentary: Heavy press expected to start production in Q4 FY27, with an SOP around 8,000 tonnes. Initial volumes of about Rs 50-100 crore are expected from existing parts moving across; further investment of up to Rs 2,500 crore was mentioned in the Q&A.

segments.name: Fasteners/Abhinav (as named in transcript)
segments.commentary: Volumes were cited at 3,000-4,000 units per month, with capacity expansion still under consideration. Transcript is unclear on the exact product.

guidance_outlook: Management stated that the company plans to reach about Rs 2,400-2,500 crore turnover and cross 100,000 tonnes in sales volume, though the timeframe was not clear in the transcript.
Management said FY28 and beyond should show significant growth, subject to macro conditions and cycle, with heavy press order discussions positive.
Debt levels are expected to stay roughly flat at the current level through the year-end, with about Rs 75 crore more capex planned in H2 on top of about Rs 150 crore spent in H1 on capex.
Management agreed to consider giving annual guidance as outperformance versus industry growth, but did not commit to it.
Margin expectation described as positive over the next few years, driven by efficiency, but no numbers given.
capex_capacity: Capacity rose from 1.20 lakh to 1.30 lakh tonnes in Q2 FY27 after adding a 4,000-tonne press at the Vizianagaram plant; management noted this is still tracked on an annualised basis.
Heavy press (approx. 8,000-tonne SOP) expected to start production in Q4 FY27; some parts to move after OEM qualification, with ramp-up timing still open.
Machining utilisation around 75-80%; new machining lines being added, with management targeting roughly Rs 2,400 crore revenue-generation capacity in the mix discussed.
Capex of about Rs 150 crore in H1 and about Rs 75 crore planned for H2 FY27 (as stated).
Management acknowledged project delays of about 16-18 months on some capex, tied to customer qualification and foundation work; the transcript is unclear on exact months.
demand_pricing: North America Class 8 truck demand is strong from April onwards; management attributed part of this to pre-buy ahead of emission norm changes, which it expects to fade, with replacement demand as the underlying base.
Europe is largely replacement-driven and is growing for the company as its share rises.

Heavy forging competition: Bharat Forge and Ramkrishna Forgings are adding heavy presses; management says it started from zero heavy forging seven years ago and sees growing Indian share as fleets age and scrappage policy evolves.
Realisation improvement of about 19% sequentially was raised by an analyst; management did not clearly confirm whether it reflected steel pass-through or mix.

qa_highlights.question: Will management guide on outperformance versus industry growth rather than absolute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will work out how to compare itself with industry growth and see where it stands; no commitment was made.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue can current capacity support before new capex is needed, and what is utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1.30 lakh tonnes (annualised basis), with machining utilisation around 75-80%; new machining lines are being added to reach a target revenue level for the planned job mix.

qa_highlights.question: How long do OEM qualifications take for heavy parts, and what is the heavy press ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Some parts can move directly to the press; roughly Rs 50-100 crore of existing parts could move, with further capex of up to Rs 2,500 crore needed later. Orders are available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of debt and where will debt end the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is 5.42%; overall debt is expected to remain around the current level through year-end, with about Rs 150 crore capex in H1 and about Rs 75 crore planned for H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a capex delay, and why has capitalisation lagged spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays were attributed to foundation work and customer qualification on one or two projects; over three years about Rs 800 crore was spent versus Rs 380 crore capitalised, per the analyst's figure.

qa_highlights.question: Which products are the company's core leadership areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Top three product families were said to make up about 45% of revenue, with the top five above 55%; management said capacity is being debottlenecked to defend these.

risks_watch: Capitalisation lag: about Rs 380 crore capitalised against about Rs 800 crore spent over three years, which pressures return on capital.
Heavy press ramp: production start in Q4 FY27 depends on OEM qualification; follow-on investment of up to Rs 2,500 crore is still undecided.
North America Class 8 demand may fall after pre-buy ends ahead of emission norms; cyclicality is a risk for the 85% CV-linked revenue base.
Competition in heavy forgings from Bharat Forge and Ramkrishna Forgings, which are adding heavy presses.
Transcript quality is poor; several figures (realisation unit, capacity dates, debt guidance) need verification against the official filing.
summary.management_tone: Management was constructive on the heavy press and North America/Europe demand, but cautious on timing and capex, saying new investment is subject to macro conditions and cycle. It was evasive on guidance format and machining capacity totals, and it acknowledged capex delays.
key_quotes: The heavy press, as I have been saying in most of the calls, remains largely unsolved.
Our capacity has gone up from lakh and 20,000 to lakh and 30,000 tonnes, only in Q2.

adds.what: 4,000-tonne press at Vizianagaram plant (installed capacity 1.20 to 1.30 lakh t/yr, annualised)
Heavy press (approx. 8,000-tonne SOP) for non-auto parts

growth.why: Management cited a target of about Rs 2,400-2,500 crore turnover and over 100,000 tonnes with no timeline, backed partly by the 4,000-tonne press added in Q2 and an 8,000-tonne heavy press due in Q4 FY27 (initial Rs 50-100 crore), while the transcript is garbled and realisation and capacity figures are uncertain.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management described margins as positive over the next few years driven by efficiency, but gave no numbers; the reported 19% sequential realisation rise was unconfirmed and capitalisation lags spend (Rs 380 cr capitalised vs Rs 800 cr spent over 3 years).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 4,000-tonne press added in Q2 lifted capacity from 1.20 to 1.30 lakh tonnes, and the 8,000-tonne-SOP heavy press is guided to start production in Q4 FY27, though OEM qualification and ramp timing remain open.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets over 100,000 tonnes and Rs 2,400-2,500 crore turnover (no timeline), H1 FY27 sales were about 44,000 tonnes, and orders are said to be available for the heavy press, with Europe share rising to about 16.5%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 75-80% and new machining lines are being added, while up to Rs 2,500 crore of further heavy-press investment is mentioned but undecided and management is cautious on timing and macro conditions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to commit to annual guidance, saying only that it would consider outperformance versus industry growth, and it cited macro and cycle dependence for FY28.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: North America Class 8 demand is partly pre-buy ahead of emission norms that management expects to fade, and the company acknowledged 16-18 month capex delays tied to customer qualification and foundation work.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The heavy (non-auto) press with an 8,000-tonne SOP is due to start in Q4 FY27 with initial Rs 50-100 crore of existing parts moving across, and fasteners/Abhinav capacity expansion is still under consideration.

rows.label: Heavy press orders in hand
rows.why: Management said orders are available and heavy press order discussions are positive, with about Rs 50-100 crore of existing parts expected to move to the press at start-up.

rows.label: Capex capitalisation lag
rows.why: About Rs 380 crore capitalised against about Rs 800 crore spent over three years, with Rs 75 crore more capex planned in H2 FY27 and debt held flat, so capitalisation must catch up for returns to improve.

rows.label: Debt held flat through FY27 end
rows.why: Management expects total debt to stay around the current level through year-end at an average cost of debt of 5.42%, with capex of about Rs 150 crore in H1 and Rs 75 crore in H2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the heavy press, orders and North America/Europe replacement demand, but cautious on capex timing, macro dependence and guidance format; analysts pressed on realisation, capitalisation lag and capex delays.
